purpose: Monomethyl fumarate is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including clinically isolated syndrome and relapsing-remitting MS. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows down the worsening of the disease. This medicine can help protect your brain and nervous system from further damage.
how_it_works: This medicine works by activating a natural protective pathway in your body called the Nrf2 pathway, which helps protect your nerve cells from damage and inflammation. It also helps calm down an overactive immune system that is mistakenly attacking the nerves. Think of it as giving your body's own defense and repair system a helpful boost.
common_side_effects: Flushing (feeling hot, red, or tingly in the face or body) is very common, especially when you first start. Stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, or stomach pain can also happen. Taking this medicine with food can help reduce these stomach side effects.
warnings: This medicine can lower your white blood cell count, which means your body may have a harder time fighting infections — your doctor will check your blood regularly. A rare but serious brain infection called PML has been associated with similar medications, so report any new or unusual symptoms like confusion, vision changes, or weakness right away. Do not take this medicine if you are allergic to fumarates, and tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 190 mg taken by mouth twice a day, with food to reduce stomach side effects. Your doctor may have you start at the same dose or may adjust based on how you tolerate it. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and do not stop without talking to them first.
